subject: Promptset A/B contingency checkpoint + acceptance map
messages:
From: Sara Montgomery <sara@acmeai.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: mlops@acme.ai
Date: Sun, 19 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observed quality delta on promptset-B in production (sample attached)

Hi Grace,

We started a slow rollout of Promptset-B yesterday and our monitoring picked up a spike in hallucination-type errors on product descriptions (examples attached). Rate is small (~0.6% of calls) but the errors are high-severity for our downstream customers. We paused rollouts at 3am PT and wanted to loop you in while we triage.

Attached: sample-responses-19may.json (redacted)

Can your team flag any recent model variants, quant params, or infra changes that could correlate? Happy to hop on a quick call.

—Sara
Principal ML Ops, Acme AI
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Montgomery <sara@acmeai.com>, mlops@acme.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 May 2029 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed quality delta on promptset-B in production (sample attached)

Thanks for the heads-up, Sara — and thanks for the samples. We're treating this as a high-priority eval incident. Short answers up-front: no infra-wide kernel changes on our side in the last 48h; we pushed a promptset normalization tweak for B two nights ago and a small quant profile change to the 8-bit rollout last week.

Planned immediate steps from Redwood: 
- Marissa will run a fast regression eval across the failing set and the control promptset-A snapshot.
- Karthik will validate the quant profile differences and confirm whether the variant is compatible with the model family used by Acme.
- Jonas will prepare an A/B contingency plan with clear acceptance gates to decide rollback vs. continued rollout.
- I will coordinate with Acme on short-term mitigations (prefix routing to A for high-risk endpoints).

Can your team confirm the customer-facing severity threshold you want enforced (e.g., block rollout when >0.5% of calls are high-severity hallucinations for 60m)? Also share any expanded sample sets if available.

I'll set up a 30-minute sync at 10:30 PT and attach a working checklist.

Best,
Grace
Lead, Model Quality Programs
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 May 2029 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed quality delta on promptset-B in production (sample attached)

On Sun, May 19, 2029 at 09:40 AM Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Planned immediate steps from Redwood: 
> - Marissa will run a fast regression eval across the failing set and the control promptset-A snapshot.

Quick update: I'm running the regression now against the curated failure set Sara provided + an expanded 800-example sample from Acme's UI logs. Early signal: the precision drop is concentrated on a handful of intent slices (product spec generation with nested bullet lists). I'm attaching a short PDF summary with examples and signal counts.

Preliminary hypothesis: the normalization tweak to Promptset-B changed a conditioning token ordering that interacts poorly with the current decoding temperature on that workload. If that holds, acceptable mitigations are: revert normalization for B, or temporarily route high-risk endpoints to Promptset-A while we iterate.

I'll post a full table of pass/fail counts in ~45m.

—Marissa
Senior Eval Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 May 2029 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed quality delta on promptset-B in production (sample attached)

Agree with Marissa's hypothesis. I validated the quant profile matrix and there are no mismatches, but the recent normalization tweak also introduced a different tokenization boundary for a small set of tokens used heavily in Acme's product descriptions. That boundary change can amplify decoding artifacts at certain temperatures.

Action items from infra/model side: 
- I'll stage a rollback of the normalization change to the Promptset-B slot in canary (no full rollback yet) so we can test whether signal disappears.
- If rollback removes the signal, we propose a targeted A/B: keep B for low-risk buckets, route high-risk endpoints to A for 24–48h while we re-evaluate normalization and temperature defaults.

ETA for the staged rollback test: 2 hours (by 12:30 PT).

Karthik
Principal Applied ML Engineer
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Sara Montgomery <sara@acmeai.com>
Date: Sun, 19 May 2029 12:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed quality delta on promptset-B in production (sample attached)

Thanks team — standing up the contingency map now. High-level proposal (for Acme sign-off):

1) Short-term guardrail (immediate):
   - Route Acme production calls for endpoints tagged "spec-gen" to Promptset-A.
   - Keep Promptset-B active for non-spec-gen buckets to preserve rollout momentum.
   - Threshold: if high-severity hallucinations >0.4% over a rolling 45m window across spec-gen, auto-fallback completes to A and rollout paused.

2) Test (12–36h):
   - Run canary with rollback-normalization enabled and run Marissa's regression suite continuously.
   - Track two acceptance metrics: (a) hallucination rate on spec-gen, (b) semantic correctness score delta (eval metric). Acceptance if hallucination reduction to <=0.25% and semantic correctness delta <=0.5 points vs baseline.

3) Post-test actions:
   - If acceptance gates met: incrementally resume rollout with 10% daily increases and continued monitoring.
   - If failure: full rollback of Promptset-B and retrospective with Acme + product to determine invariant changes.

Attachments: ab-contingency-checklist-v1.xlsx (checklist + gate definitions)

Sara — can you confirm you accept the thresholds above or propose alternate numbers? We'll stand by for your approval and can trigger the immediate routing change once you sign off.

Jonas
Head of Eval Orchestration
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Montgomery <sara@acmeai.com>, mlops@acme.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed quality delta on promptset-B in production (sample attached)

Thanks everyone for the fast turnaround. 

Summary of where we landed after the staged rollback test:
- Karthik's rollback-normalization staging reduced the spec-gen hallucination rate from 0.62% -> 0.18% in the 2hr canary window.
- Marissa's regression counts show semantic correctness returned to within 0.3 points of baseline.
- Runbook checks in ab-contingency-checklist-v1.xlsx passed.

Next steps agreed with Acme:
1) Immediate: route spec-gen endpoints to Promptset-A for next 24h while we run an extended 24h canary with the normalized Promptset-B variant.
2) If 24h canary remains stable and acceptance metrics hold, resume rollout to 20% traffic on May 22 with daily increments and monitoring.
3) Owner assignments: Marissa (signal monitoring), Karthik (model changes), Jonas (gate enforcement), Grace (account coordination).

Sara — thank you for the quick sample sets and the clear severity threshold. If anything regresses overnight, please ping me directly and we'll escalate to an on-call incident.

Best,
Grace
Lead, Model Quality Programs
Redwood Inference
